## Multiple Choice Questions

**1.** Why does Guided Tutorial C.1 upload CharlesRiver.xlsx instead of reading it from a folder on your computer, as Tutorial 13.1 does?

A.  The service cannot read Excel Tables, only the worksheets that hold them
B.  Uploading converts the workbook into CSV files, which the service loads faster
C.  Power Query Online reads the workbook from a copy in your OneDrive for work or school
D.  Uploading turns off the detection of column types from the first rows

**2.** In Power Query Online, the InvoiceDate column of SalesInvoice shows five-digit numbers. What explains it, and what should you do?

A.  The workbook stores it as an Excel date, a count of days, and Power Query Online reads the number; set the column's type to Date
B.  The upload damaged the workbook's dates; upload the file again under another name
C.  The column holds document numbers that were placed under the wrong heading; remove it with Choose columns
D.  Power Query Online shows every date as a number until the model is created; leave it as it is

**3.** You want Tutorial 13.2's cards, but the Visualizations pane of the report editor has no Card. What should you do?

A.  Build the four totals with a table visual, because the service has no card visual
B.  Switch the report from Editing view to Reading view, where the card appears
C.  Open the semantic model in Editing mode and add the card there
D.  Click the … below the visual types and choose Restore default visuals

**4.** You close a model in the browser, and the DAX query tab that held your tests is gone when you open the model again. What explains it?

A.  The query had an error, so the service removed its tab
B.  DAX query view in the browser discards its tabs on close, so the tests belong in a text file
C.  The model was open in Viewing mode, where query tabs are never saved
D.  The report that reads the model was saved after the query was written

**5.** With a card selected, you select the check box of SalesInvoiceID in the SalesInvoiceLine table, and the card splits into thousands of small cards. Why?

A.  The card visual shows one card per row of any table it reads
B.  A key that a relationship uses is set not to summarize, so it went to Categories; drag it into Value and choose Count (Distinct)
C.  SalesInvoiceID is a text column, which a card cannot count
D.  The year slicer was not set to Single select, so the card repeats for each year

**6.** A line chart of discounts by month falls steadily from left to right, and its axis reads 2026-10, 2026-09, 2026-11, and so on. What happened?

A.  The promotions really declined across the year, and the chart shows it
B.  The Month column is text, which a line chart cannot order
C.  The chart lost its date table when the report was saved
D.  The chart is sorted by its values; sort it by Month, ascending, from its More options

**7.** You add a table with Enter data in Power Query Online, opened from the model editor's Transform data. What applies the new table to the model?

A.  Home > Close & Apply, as in Power BI Desktop
B.  Refresh on the model editor's ribbon
C.  Save, at the bottom right of Power Query Online
D.  Create a semantic model only, from the arrow beside Create a report

**8.** Guided Tutorial C.1 sets the type of Discount by hand, as Tutorial 13.1 does. Why is that still needed in Power Query Online?

A.  Power Query Online also types each column from its first 200 rows, where every Discount is zero
B.  The browser rounds every decimal column to two places unless it is typed
C.  Power Query Online reads every number in a workbook as text until it is typed
D.  The Key Measures table needs a decimal column for every rate
